newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share volumes jump 40 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German share volumes jump 40 percent in 1996.

text.p: The German stock exchange on Monday celebrated a record 1996, with the DAX-30 share index 28 percent above its level at the end of 1995 and share trading volume up 40.5 percent to 2,434 billion marks ($1,564 billion).
Dealers said share trading was boosted by low interest rates and the successful flotation of Deutsche Telekom AG, Europe's biggest-ever initial public offering, in November.
Business was also good on the debt market and for futures and options.
The Deutsche Telekom float offered the opportunity to woo small investors away from their beloved bonds.
A greater interest in managed equity funds also helped ease the shift from debt, long perceived to be relatively risk-free, to higher-return but often riskier, equities, they said.

The busiest month of the year for shares was March, when turnover was around 286 billion marks. The Telekom flotation boosted stock exchange turnover in November, normally a quiet month, to 249.3 billion marks from 136.2 billion a year earlier.
Deutsche Telekom, traded from November 18, was the most heavily traded stock in November with 34.6 billion marks of its shares changing hands.

For the overall cash market, the busiest month in the year was January, with total turnover of 967.5 billion marks, of which around 724 billion marks came from debt. Overall turnover in the German bond market in 1996 was 6,550 billion marks.

The German futures and options exchange DTB registered a 33 percent increase in volumes traded for the year to 77.3 million contracts, which the bourse said was ahead of the performance of the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange and the MATIF market in Paris.

"The 33 percent growth rate seen on the DTB is clearly ahead of other European futures and options exchanges. To the end of November LIFFE saw a 25 percent increase and MATIF saw a turnover drop of three percent in the year," the German bourse operating company Deutsche Boerse said in a statement.
Futures alone registered a 63 percent increase to 40.3 million traded contracts, while the sale of options increased 10.5 percent to 36.9 million contracts.
"With this volume increase, the DTB has replaced the MATIF as the number two futures exchange in Europe," Deutsche Boerse said.
For 1997, the bourse is looking to its electronic expertise to continue its recent run.

"The dealing structure of the future is a network. We are following this route with the futures and options market DTB and have it with the cash market through the IBIS (electronic trading system) already," Joerg Franke, board member of Deutsche Boerse, said in a recent interview with Reuters.
The DAX index closed the last bourse session of the year on Monday at 2,888.69 points, compared with 2,253.88 a year earlier.
